clue.text: A father receives thanks from Hollywood dancer

indicators.note: the father takes in the word for thanks, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal
TA is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A dad is thanked by a famous film dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, British slang for thanks, is a crossword regular. Fred Astaire was the Hollywood star of dance musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was the celebrated tap and ballroom star of Hollywood musicals.

clue.text: Getting better at consulting reference books

definitions.meaning: improving, as in prospects that are on the rise
searching for an entry in a dictionary or encyclopedia

explanation.surface: Someone is improving at looking things up in reference works.
explanation.definitionFit: Things improving are said to be on the rise; to check a dictionary entry is to search for a word in it.

clue.text: Indicate that it's not held by Scottish banker

indicators.note: the word not is gripped inside the river, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Dee flows through Aberdeen in Scotland
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a Scottish bank is not holding something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish banker' suggests a bank or bank employee; in crosswords a banker is a river, here one in Aberdeenshire. The words 'that it's' are only link.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to signify or mark out, a synonym of indicate.

clue.text: Large number of handouts distributed

indicators.note: spread around, so the letters of handouts are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A great many leaflets were passed around.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand is ten hundreds, a sizeable figure.

clue.text: Ill effects of the night before

definitions.text: Ill effects of the night before

parts.words: Ill effects of the night before
parts.note: the hangover felt next day after a heavy evening of drinking, named by when it strikes

explanation.surface: A description of feeling rough after a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for the hangover suffered the day following heavy drinking.

clue.text: Excel, but not in a study session

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a class is a lesson, a period of study

explanation.surface: Someone shines, though they were absent from a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is only a link here; the definition is the verb at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel over rivals is to surpass them by a wide margin.

clue.text: Middle-distance runner has to beat it

parts.note: has is shortened to 's, giving the letter S
Steve Cram was a British world-champion middle-distance runner of the 1980s

explanation.surface: An athlete is obliged to defeat a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram, the British 1500m runner, is CRAM; 'has' contracted to 's gives S, which goes before him. 'beat it' looks like defeating someone but is slang for leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang commands to go away quickly.

clue.text: Ken and Anne produce cotton

indicators.note: the two names are made to yield something new, so their letters are reworked together

explanation.surface: A couple named Ken and Anne grow cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' rearranges the letters of KEN and ANNE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a buff-coloured cotton cloth originally from Nanjing in China.

clue.text: Men embraced by a woman on the beach

indicators.note: being hugged by something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Some men are hugged by a woman at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a crossword staple for men in the army. 'embraced by' puts OR inside SHE, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land at the water's edge rather than at sea is what the adverb describes.

clue.text: One the RN resolved to induct as bishop

indicators.note: something resolved is broken down and remade, so these letters are recast

parts.note: the Royal Navy, part of the anagram material

explanation.surface: The Navy decided to install a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' reads as decided, but it rearranges ONE THE RN.
explanation.definitionFit: A new bishop is formally installed on his throne, the cathedra.

clue.text: There's scope for development here

parts.note: scope means space, and development is of photographic film, done in a room with no light

explanation.surface: A place offering room to grow, as a careers advisor might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers process film in a lightless room set aside for that work.

clue.text: Household junk fellers value

definitions.meaning: unwanted furniture and clutter stored about a house
the cut timber that tree-fellers prize

explanation.surface: Domestic clutter is prized by tree-cutters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted old furniture is stored clutter in British usage; timber sawn from felled trees is what loggers are after.

clue.text: Great European splendour

parts.note: grand means great or magnificent
EUR is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A great European's magnificence is praised.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is magnificence, impressive splendid display.

clue.text: Baby bird is snuggling up

definitions.meaning: a chick too young to leave its nest
cuddling close, settling comfortably against someone

explanation.surface: A chick is cuddling up close.
explanation.definitionFit: A young chick not yet out of its nest; cuddling close is settling cosily into someone.

clue.text: Anyway, that's most foolish

definitions.meaning: at any rate, in any case
having the smallest amount of good sense

explanation.surface: A shrug at whatever is the silliest thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at any rate; split in two it says having the smallest amount of sense.

clue.text: Mother and I get a length of cloth

parts.note: mater is Latin for mother, used jocularly in Britain

explanation.surface: A mother and child buy fabric by the metre.
explanation.walkthrough: MATER is old public-school slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Material is fabric, woven stuff for making clothes.

clue.text: Minister gets a place in housing queue

indicators.note: the line encloses the other letters, as a building holds its occupants

parts.note: a chain is a line of people or things one after another
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A clergyman is found a spot in a waiting list for council housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing queue' reads as a waiting list for council homes, but 'housing' is the container signal and 'queue' alone gives the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman serving an institution, a minister of religion.

clue.text: I help to resettle an old soldier

indicators.note: to resettle is to put back in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone offers to help a veteran find a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resettle' rearranges the letters of I HELP TO; 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoplite was a heavily armed infantryman of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Not little rock, but a place in Colorado

definitions.meaning: a big stone, the opposite of a small rock

explanation.surface: Not Little Rock, Arkansas, but a city in Colorado.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Rock is the capital of Arkansas, so the clue seems to contrast two US cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A large stone is far from a small pebble; the Colorado city is home to the state university.

clue.text: Property stolen by top-class sniper

parts.note: goods are possessions, property
hot is slang for stolen

explanation.surface: An expert marksman makes off with possessions.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, it is praise for an excellent marksman.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack marksman is someone whose aim is consistently excellent.

clue.text: Go on and on and on

definitions.text: Go on and on and on

parts.words: Go on and on and on
parts.note: the repetition itself acts out continuing to excess, doing too much of something

explanation.surface: A complaint about someone who never stops talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry something to excess, beyond what is needed, is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Understanding how to get an aerial photo?

definitions.meaning: comprehension, as in quick on the grasp

definitions.text: how to get an aerial photo?
definitions.meaning: split in two, a picture shot from up high

explanation.surface: A question about grasping how pictures are shot from the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Quickness of grasp is comprehension; shooting a picture from high up is a snap from above.

clue.text: Fruit that's very soft is steeped in stout

indicators.note: soaking in a drink means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: stout is a dark beer, broadly a kind of ale
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: Fruit so mushy it has been soaked in dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very soft' reads as mushy fruit but is a musical dynamic marking, pianissimo. Stout is loosely treated as a kind of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The apple is a common orchard fruit.

clue.text: Unrestricted option to grant probate

definitions.meaning: to release a dead person's testament so it can be carried out

explanation.surface: A choice without limits on settling an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconstrained choice is the faculty of deciding for oneself; granting probate releases a testament for execution.

clue.text: Describe precise location of cash dispenser

definitions.meaning: a machine where you enter your personal identification number

explanation.surface: A request to say exactly where the cashpoint is.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify exactly is to locate with precision; a cashpoint is where you key in your personal number.

clue.text: Crockery for a man in Norfolk town

indicators.note: the man is placed inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Buying plates for a chap living in an English market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes are plates and bowls, collectively crockery.

clue.text: Derisive remark about flourishing retailer

indicators.note: the jeer goes around the other word, placed about it

parts.note: a jeer is a mocking taunt
well means healthy, thriving

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is mocked for doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is broad: this retailer sells gems and watches.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeweller is a shopkeeper selling rings, watches and gems.
